text:
Alex DeBrincat grew up in Farmington Hills and scored 41 goals for his hometown team last season. This November has been harder. He is pointless in six straight games on 5.1 expected points, and the chances have thinned out too, so our numbers don't call it bad luck: 3.2 expected goals on his own shots over his last ten, against 4.0 usual. Yahoo Sports summed it up as "DeBrincat Has Gone Quiet as Red Wings Lose Four Straight."

The season as a whole is healthier than the slump. He has 72 shots and 8.4 expected goals (the quality of his chances) for 7 goals, and at five on five Detroit takes 57% of the expected goals with him on, 9.7 points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him 6th among 401 forwards last season at 3.5 wins, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put him in the 98th percentile for chances from the slot.

On Nov. 12 he dropped the gloves with Sam Bennett while Florida came back from 4 to 1 down. Fans noticed. What we'd watch is the shot volume: if it returns, the points usually follow.
